author: product-requirements-expert
title: Reader can narrow the veterinarian directory to one specialty
summary: Both published forms of the veterinarian directory - the browser page and the machine-readable form - can be narrowed to the veterinarians holding one named specialty. Naming no specialty leaves each form as it is today.
acceptance_criteria: given the clinic's veterinarians, when the machine-readable form is requested without a specialty, then every veterinarian is returned with the specialties each holds
given a specialty one or more veterinarians hold, when either form is requested for that specialty, then only those veterinarians are listed
given a filtered directory longer than one page, when the human-readable form is requested, then the narrowed list is paged, not the full one
given a specialty name differing from the stored name only by letter case, when either form is requested for it, then it matches
given part of a specialty name rather than the whole name, when either form is requested for it, then no veterinarian matches
given a specialty no veterinarian holds, when either form is requested for it, then the request succeeds and the directory is empty
given a specialty that is empty or entirely spaces, when either form is requested, then the result matches the same request with no specialty named
given no specialty named, when either form is requested, then the directory is listed whole, a page at a time in the human-readable form
non_goals: free-text search for veterinarians, pets, or visits (NG-9, narrowed 2026-08-05)
a specialty picker or any new control on the directory page
notes: Product-owner decisions of record: (1) the filter value is carried on both surfaces as a query parameter named 'specialty' - the name is fixed, its handling is the design stage's call; (2) the machine-readable form is reinstated as a supported surface under this new ID, REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its ID is not reused, and the removal previously pending against that route is cancelled; (3) NG-9 is narrowed rather than withdrawn - see docs/adr/2026-08-05-non-goal-veterinarian-search.md. Open and deliberately unsettled: whether a real specialty name carrying leading or trailing spaces is trimmed (owner search trims). Empty-or-all-spaces is settled and behaves as no specialty. docs/adr/README.md index row for the new ADR is owned by system-design-expert; system-design.md still lists the machine-readable route as debt serving no requirement (line 207) and as REQ-VET-001-only in the component table - both need reconciling there.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice extends the existing vet feature package: no new package, no new type, no new dependency. Both routes stay on VetController, and the narrowing is a second read on VetRepository, mirroring the paged derived query OwnerRepository already uses for owner search. What is new is the rule for how the narrowing is expressed, because the project's incumbent habit - reaching case-insensitivity through the database (H2 column type, MySQL collation, PostgreSQL functional index) - already produced a per-vendor divergence (REQ-OWN-002, system-design.md Known Defects). The specialty comparison therefore folds case in the query (Spring Data IgnoreCase, compiling to upper() on both operands), so it holds on all three vendors. Second new rule: the narrowed reads carry no @Cacheable, while the unfiltered reads keep theirs - a filter value is caller-supplied text and the 'vets' cache has no size limit or eviction. Both rules are recorded in docs/system-design.md Persistence and in docs/adr/2026-08-05-specialty-filter-in-the-query.md.
integration_points: VetRepository gains two reads narrowed by specialty name - one Page<Vet> with a Pageable for the HTML route, one Collection<Vet> for the serialized route. Neither is annotated @Cacheable; the existing findAll pair is untouched.

VetController normalizes the optional 'specialty' request parameter at the boundary (strip, then blank means absent) and chooses the narrowed or the unfiltered read. No matching logic in the controller.

vetList.html pagination links must carry the specialty forward, built with the Thymeleaf link-expression parameter form @{/vets.html(page=...,specialty=...)} rather than string-concatenated query text - the builder URL-encodes and omits a null parameter, so the absent case renders today's links.
The controller's model gains a specialty attribute solely so the pagination links can carry it. Nothing echoes the value into page text; the directory grows no new control (PRD non-goal).
Vets is unchanged: a narrowed serialized response is the same wrapper with fewer entries, and a no-match response is HTTP 200 with an empty vetList.

patterns.description: paged derived query taking a Pageable - the shape the narrowed vet read follows
boundary normalization of an optional search parameter, including strip() - the precedent the specialty normalization follows
existing findPaginated/addPaginationModel helper pair - the narrowed read threads through it rather than growing a parallel path

risks.risk: VetControllerTests runs under @WebMvcTest with a @MockitoBean VetRepository, so it cannot prove case-insensitive whole-name matching or the no-partial-match rule - a stubbed repository returns whatever the test says it returns. The eight prd-entry test names alone would leave the slice's central rule unverified.
risks.mitigation: Prove the matching rule at the repository in ClinicServiceTests (@DataJpaTest, real VetRepository, seeded radiology/surgery/dentistry): whole-name match, case-varied match, partial name matching nothing, unheld name returning empty. The controller tests keep their scope - parameter binding, blank-as-absent, paging of the narrowed list, and the two response shapes.

risks.risk: architecture-principles.md is explicit that a new rule added to a controller is a fresh violation, not covered by the existing controller-logic deviation. Filtering or case-folding in VetController would be exactly that.
risks.mitigation: The controller does binding-time normalization and read selection only. The matching rule lives entirely in the derived query name.

risks.risk: Caching the narrowed read would key an unbounded cache on attacker-supplied text over an unauthenticated route.
risks.mitigation: No @Cacheable on the narrowed reads (ADR). Recorded as a threat-model row in system-design.md so a reviewer sees the choice rather than an omission.

risks.risk: Vet.specialties is a ManyToMany with FetchType.EAGER, and a Page over a query that joins the collection can degrade into in-memory pagination (Hibernate HHH90003004) or duplicate rows.
risks.mitigation: The predicate is an equality on one specialty name, so a vet matches at most one join row and no distinct is needed; the eager collection loads by secondary select rather than a fetch join, keeping paging in SQL. Verify no in-memory-pagination warning appears when the narrowed page test runs, and treat a widening of the predicate as a fresh design question.

risks.risk: Filtered requests bypass the cache, so a route that was previously always cache-served now reaches the database on every filtered call.
risks.mitigation: Accepted and recorded in the ADR's Consequences. The directory is small and the unfiltered path - the one every browser hits by default - is unchanged.

notes: Design call on the question the PRD left deliberately open (trimming a real specialty name that carries leading or trailing spaces): the value is stripped at the web boundary and an empty result is treated as absent, so one normalization rule covers both the settled blank case and the open trimming case. This matches owner search (OwnerController:98-103) and stays inside the handling latitude the product owner assigned to the design stage; it adds no behavior the PRD's acceptance criteria contradict. || Three reconciliations applied to durable memory: (1) the Known Defects row 'The machine-readable veterinarian route serves no requirement' is removed - the route is a supported surface under REQ-VET-003 and its pending removal is cancelled; (2) the Contracts table now maps VetController and VetRepository to REQ-VET-001 plus REQ-VET-003 and Vets to REQ-VET-003, which also makes the section's standing claim that only three kinds of contract carry an Implements value of '-' true again; (3) docs/adr/README.md gains index rows for both 2026-08-05 ADRs - the product-owned non-goal ADR and the new one written here. Security Context inputs, the threat model, and Open Question 5 were updated for accuracy alongside. || No design-doc-autofix records exist in the handoff log, so the autofix audit is a no-op for this dispatch. || Vocabulary check: 'Veterinarian' in prose, 'Vet' as the code short form, 'Specialty' for the filtered attribute - all canonical in docs/ubiquitous-language.md. The Vets wrapper stays a code symbol and is never called a domain concept.

author: code-quality-reviewer
approved_aspects: Case folding for the specialty match happens in the query via Spring Data's IgnoreCase derived-query keyword (UPPER() on both operands), not database collation, per the ADR and design-block; VetRepository:298-299 and the ADR both state this explicitly

The two narrowed reads (findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase, with and without Pageable) carry no @Cacheable, while the pre-existing findAll()/findAll(Pageable) pair keeps @Cacheable("vets") unchanged - VetRepository.java:44-56 vs 70-83

VetController normalizes the optional specialty parameter once at the boundary (namedSpecialtyOrNull: strip, then blank-to-null) and keeps the matching rule entirely in the derived query name, avoiding a fresh controller-logic violation per architecture-principles.md
Javadoc on both new repository methods documents the case-folding behavior and the caching decision inline, giving a future reader the rationale without needing the ADR

vetList.html's null-safe ternary link expressions correctly avoid the empty-parameter trap a bare @{...(specialty=${specialty})} would introduce when specialty is null, matching the corrected design-block guidance
./gradlew checkFormat, compileJava, and checkstyleMain all pass clean on the change set

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: No injection surface: the specialty reaches the store only through the Spring Data derived queries findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String) and (String, Pageable) in VetRepository. Query derivation binds the name as a JPQL parameter and expresses IgnoreCase as an upper()/lower() comparison; no @Query, no string concatenation, and no dynamic sort or property reference anywhere in the change set. Grep across src/main for the concatenation class found no other instance.

Pageable is constructed server-side in VetController.findPaginated via PageRequest.of, not bound from the request, so the derived query gains no caller-controlled property-reference surface through a sort parameter.

Output encoding holds on both echo paths. The specialty is never rendered as text: vetList.html uses it solely inside link expressions @{/vets.html(page=..., specialty=${specialty})}, which URL-encode the parameter value, and th:href additionally HTML-escapes the attribute. A payload such as "><script> is emitted as an encoded query value, not as markup or a new attribute. The change also replaces the previous preprocessed literal URLs (@{'/vets.html?page=__${i}__'}) with parameterized link expressions, removing the pattern that would have concatenated a value into a URL string. The /vets JSON route does not echo the parameter at all.

The caching decision recorded in the design-block and in the docs/system-design.md threat-model row is honored in code: both findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase overloads carry no @Cacheable, while both unfiltered findAll overloads keep @Cacheable("vets"). The vets cache key space therefore stays closed to callers even though CacheConfiguration declares the cache with no size limit and no eviction.

Boundary normalization in VetController.namedSpecialtyOrNull collapses null and blank to a single absent-value representation before the read, so no empty-string filter reaches the query and the template's null branch is reachable and correct.

No new data exposure: the narrowed reads return the same Vet fields already published by the unfiltered directory on the same unauthenticated routes, and specialty names are already displayed beside every veterinarian. No PII or credential material is added to any response, log, or error path.

No hardcoded secrets in the change set. The only diff hits for credential vocabulary are pre-existing prose in the docs/system-design.md security context describing the committed database-credential defaults, which this slice neither introduces nor changes.

Supply chain unchanged: build.gradle, settings.gradle, and the gradle/ wrapper metadata are absent from the change set, so no dependency was added, upgraded, or downgraded and this slice introduces no new CVE surface.

risks.risk: Vet.specialties is a ManyToMany with FetchType.EAGER, and a Page over a query that joins the collection can degrade into in-memory pagination (Hibernate HHH90003004) or duplicate rows.

risks.risk: Filtered requests bypass the cache, so a route that was previously always cache-served now reaches the database on every filtered call.

blast_radius.note: Ten files, but the production reach is one feature package (VetController, VetRepository) plus its own template; no sensitive path, no schema, no dependency, no shared configuration, and the owner-side pagination template is untouched. semantic_surprise.note: Two behavior changes the 'add a specialty filter' framing does not advertise. Both vet routes were previously served wholly from the eviction-free vets cache; any caller-supplied specialty now takes a deliberately uncached database path on an unauthenticated route, and the ADR and threat table record only the cache-key-space half of that trade, not the query-load half. Separately, the template rewrite retires the Thymeleaf double-underscore preprocessing idiom on all five pagination links - verified benign, links render identically, pinned by a test - a security-relevant change riding in under a filter feature.

test_adequacy.note: Real @DataJpaTest H2 tests at the repository prove case folding, whole-name-only matching, the empty result, and paging against seeded data rather than restating the implementation, and the controller tests are red-capable: the setup stub returns a non-empty findAll page, so a controller ignoring the parameter fails the empty-directory and blank-specialty cases. reviewer_hedging.note: All four reviewers of the full high-risk battery hold approvals with empty findings lists. The round-one findings (an acceptance criterion unproven at the HTML surface, BDD naming, five over-length sentences) were each re-verified fixed in round two with traced evidence, not waived or accepted with caveats.

scope_deviation.note: namedSpecialtyOrNull strips surrounding space and so settles the trimming rule that the PRD's own newly added Open Question records as undecided - shipped, untested, and contradicted by the document in the same change set. rationale: Correct and well tested, but it moves a product boundary and quietly changes the cache posture of two public routes. Before merging, confirm you mean to support the /vets JSON surface, and settle the space-trimming rule the code decided while the PRD calls it open.
